mainTopic: The opening משנה of בבא מציעא (two people holding one item, split with a שבועה) and the גמרא's analysis of its double wording: 'I found it' and 'All of it is mine.'
overview: This amud opens מסכת בבא מציעא with a משנה about two people who both grab the same object and each claim it. When both hold a טלית and each says all of it is his, each swears he owns at least half, and they split it. If one claims all and the other claims half, only the disputed half is split, so the shares are three-quarters and one-quarter. The same rule applies to an animal that both are riding, or that one rides and one leads. If they admit each other's claims or have עדים, they split it without a שבועה. The גמרא then asks why the משנה has each person say both 'I found it' and 'All of it is mine.' First it reads them as one combined claim, and learns from the extra words that seeing an object alone does not acquire it. When the repeated 'זה אומר' shows two separate statements, רב פפא explains that the first is about a found object and the second about a purchase. The גמרא then announces that both cases are needed, and the reason comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Two people holding a garment, each claims all of it
steps.stepSummary: Two people are holding a טלית. Each says he found it and that all of it is his. Each swears he owns at least half, and they split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two people are holding a garment. One says, "I found it," and the other says, "I found it." One says, "All of it is mine," and the other says, "All of it is mine." Each one swears that he owns no less than half of it, and they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents its first and basic case: two people holding one טלית, each claiming the whole thing. בית דין has each one take a שבועה, and then they split it equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side has proof, and both are physically holding the garment, so neither one wins outright. Each swears to a share of at least half, which is what he will actually receive. The שבועה is meant to stop someone who grabbed it falsely from walking away with half for free.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding (both people have their hands on the object)

steps.confusionAlert: Each person does not swear "all of it is mine," even though that is what he claimed. He swears only that he owns no less than half, because half is the share he will actually take.

phrases.english: Two people are holding a garment,
this one says: "I found it,"
and that one says: "I found it."
This one says: "All of it is mine,"
and that one says: "All of it is mine."

phrases.aramaic: זֶה יִשָּׁבַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ פָּחוֹת מֵחֶצְיָהּ,
phrases.english: This one swears that he does not have less than half of it,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה יִשָּׁבַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ פָּחוֹת מֵחֶצְיָהּ –
phrases.english: and that one swears that he does not have less than half of it,
and they divide it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening case of the משנה and of the מסכת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two people hold a found garment and each claims all of it, each swears he owns at least half, and they split it equally.

steps.title: One claims all and the other claims half
steps.stepSummary: If one claims the whole טלית and the other claims only half, they really argue over just one half. That half is split, so the shares are three-quarters and one-quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one says, "All of it is mine," and the other says, "Half of it is mine," the one who says "All of it is mine" swears that he owns no less than three parts. The one who says "Half of it is mine" swears that he owns no less than a quarter. This one takes three parts, and that one takes a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה changes the claims in the same garment case. Now one person claims all of it and the other claims only half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person claiming half is admitting that the other half belongs to his opponent. So only one half is really in dispute, and that half is split in two. The first person ends up with half plus a quarter, which is three-quarters, and the second gets a quarter. Each swears only to the share he actually takes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that בית דין only divides what is actually disputed. Whatever one side admits goes straight to the other side.

phrases.english: This one says: "All of it is mine,"
and that one says: "Half of it is mine,"
the one who says "All of it is mine"

phrases.aramaic: יִשָּׁבַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים,
phrases.english: swears that he does not have less than three parts of it,
phrases.notes: "Three parts" means three out of four parts, which is three-quarters.

phrases.english: and the one who says "Half of it is mine"

phrases.aramaic: יִשָּׁבַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ פָּחוֹת מֵרְבִיעַ.
phrases.english: swears that he does not have less than a quarter of it.
This one takes three parts,
and that one takes a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּהּ שֶׁלִּי, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר: חֶצְיָהּ שֶׁלִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the claims from step 1: one now claims only half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one claims all and the other claims half, only the disputed half is split. The first takes three-quarters and the second takes a quarter, each with a שבועה.

steps.title: Two people on an animal, each claims all of it
steps.stepSummary: The same 50/50 rule applies to a בהמה when both are riding it, or when one rides and the other leads it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two people were riding on an animal, or one was riding and one was leading it, and this one says, "All of it is mine," and that one says, "All of it is mine," each one swears that he owns no less than half of it, and they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from a garment to an animal. It applies the same equal-split ruling when both people have some hold on the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that riding and leading are both treated as a connection to the animal. Even when one person rides and the other only leads, the two are treated the same, and they split it equally after each takes a שבועה.

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: If two people were riding on the back of an animal,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אֶחָד רוֹכֵב וְאֶחָד מַנְהִיג,
phrases.english: or one was riding and one was leading it,
this one says: "All of it is mine,"
and that one says: "All of it is mine,"

phrases.aramaic: זֶה יִשָּׁבַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ פָּחוֹת מֵחֶצְיָהּ,
phrases.english: this one swears that he does not have less than half of it,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה יִשָּׁבַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ פָּחוֹת מֵחֶצְיָהּ,
phrases.english: and that one swears that he does not have less than half of it,
and they divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ruling from step 1 to a new object, an animal, held in new ways.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two riders, or a rider and a leader, who each claim the whole animal each swear to at least half, and they split it.

steps.title: When there is admission or witnesses, no oath is needed
steps.stepSummary: If the two sides admit each other's claims, or have עדים, they split the item without any שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they admit to each other, or when they have witnesses, they divide it without an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by limiting where the שבועה applies. The oath is only needed when there is no other way to settle the claims.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides agree, or if עדים settle the facts, there is nothing left in doubt. So בית דין divides the item without a שבועה. This makes clear that the oath in the earlier cases fills a gap in proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Admit or agree to each other's claims

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's system is simple. Each person swears to the share he will take, and only the disputed part is split. Once there is admission or witnesses, no שבועה is needed at all.

phrases.english: When they admit,
phrases.notes: Each one agrees to what the other is claiming.

phrases.english: or when they have witnesses,
they divide it without an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵם מוֹדִים אוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the oath requirement from steps 1 to 3 to cases where nothing else settles the claims.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the sides admit each other's claims or have witnesses, they split the item without a שבועה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה repeat two claims?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs both 'I found it' and 'All of it is mine.' One claim should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה teach both 'This one says I found it and that one says I found it' and 'This one says all of it is mine and that one says all of it is mine'? Let it teach just one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by questioning the wording of the משנה. It looks extra, so the גמרא asks why it is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to list two separate pairs of claims. The גמרא assumes the משנה does not waste words, so either one pair should be enough. Two possible problems are on the table: repetition, or a hidden second case.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
Why do I need this? A question about extra wording
To teach (said about the משנה's wording)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why do I need [the משנה] to teach
This one says: I found it
and that one says: I found it,
this one says: All of it is mine
and that one says: All of it is mine?
Let it teach one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the opening case of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The double wording in the משנה's first case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה does not repeat itself for no reason, so two pairs of claims look unnecessary.

steps.title: It is really one combined claim
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches one claim per person: 'I found it and all of it is mine.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches one: this one says 'I found it and all of it is mine,' and that one says 'I found it and all of it is mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two phrases are not two separate cases. Each person says both parts together as one claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the משנה described two cases. The answer reads it as one case where each claim has two parts. This raises the next question: why is the second part needed?

phrases.english: It teaches one [claim]:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה אוֹמֵר אֲנִי מְצָאתִיהָ וְכוּלָּהּ שֶׁלִּי,
phrases.english: this one says: I found it and all of it is mine,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה אוֹמֵר אֲנִי מְצָאתִיהָ וְכוּלָּהּ שֶׁלִּי.
phrases.english: and that one says: I found it and all of it is mine.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: one combined claim, not two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists two separate cases
steps.terutzMaskana: Each person makes one two-part claim

steps.title: Wouldn't 'I found it' alone be enough?
steps.stepSummary: If it is one claim, why add 'all of it is mine'? 'I found it' already tells us he wants the whole thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it teach just 'I found it,' and I would know he means 'all of it is mine'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Even as one claim, the second half looks unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who says 'I found it' is obviously claiming the whole item. So 'all of it is mine' seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: And I would know (on my own)

phrases.english: But let it teach [only] 'I found it,'
and I would know that [he means] all of it is mine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6 by asking why its second part is needed
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'all of it is mine' inside the combined claim
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'I found it' already implies a claim to the whole item, so the extra words seem redundant.

steps.title: 'All of it is mine' teaches that seeing does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: Without the extra words, we might think 'I found it' means 'I saw it,' and that seeing alone makes you the owner. 'All of it is mine' teaches that seeing does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it taught only 'I found it,' I would think 'found it' means 'saw it,' and that even without picking it up, he owns it just by seeing. So it teaches 'all of it is mine,' to show that seeing does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the words 'all of it is mine' add. They block a mistaken idea about how ownership works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I found it' could be a claim of only seeing the item first. Someone might think that is enough to own it. The משנה adds 'all of it is mine' to show that each person is claiming he actually holds it, because seeing alone (רְאִיָּה) does not acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets down a basic rule of lost objects: you do not own a found item by seeing it first. It has to come into your hands.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is NOT saying seeing acquires. That was only the mistaken first idea (הֲוָה אָמֵינָא). The conclusion is that seeing does NOT acquire.

phrases.english: If it had taught [only] 'I found it,'
I would have said:
What does 'I found it' mean? I saw it.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אֲתַאי לִידֵיהּ –
phrases.english: Even though it did not come into his hand,
he acquires by mere seeing.
[So] it taught: 'All of it is mine,'
[to show] that one does not acquire by seeing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי תְּנָא אֲנִי מְצָאתִיהָ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the extra words prevent a mistaken reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'I found it' means 'I saw it,' and seeing alone acquires
steps.terutzMaskana: Seeing alone does not acquire, so each person must be claiming he holds it

steps.title: But 'found' means it came into his hands
steps.stepSummary: How can 'found' mean 'saw'? רבנאי taught that in the פסוק, 'and you found it' means it came into your hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say 'found it' means 'saw it'? Didn't רבנאי say: 'and you found it' means that it came into his hand?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the mistaken first idea of step 8. It quotes רבנאי's reading of a פסוק to show that 'finding' cannot mean only seeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8's answer depends on 'found' possibly meaning 'saw.' רבנאי showed that the תורה's word for finding means holding the object. If so, nobody would ever read 'I found it' as only seeing, and the extra words are again unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really say...? (opens a challenge)
Into his hand, into his possession

phrases.english: But can you say
that 'I found it' means 'I saw it'?
But didn't רבנאי say:
'And you found it' means that it came into his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the premise of the answer in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'found it' could mean 'saw it'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבנאי's reading of the פסוק shows that 'finding' means holding, so 'found' cannot mean only seeing.

steps.title: The משנה uses everyday speech
steps.stepSummary: True, the פסוק's 'found' means holding. But the משנה speaks like ordinary people, who say 'I found it' as soon as they see something. So 'all of it is mine' is still needed to teach that seeing does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, 'and you found it' in the פסוק means it came into his hand. But the משנה used everyday language, and once a person sees something he says 'I found it,' thinking he owns it by seeing even before it reaches his hand. So it teaches 'all of it is mine,' to show that seeing alone does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבנאי's reading of the פסוק. It explains that the משנה is not using the תורה's precise language, so the step 8 answer still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of language: the תורה's exact meaning and everyday speech. In everyday speech, people say 'I found it' when they have only spotted something. That is why the misunderstanding was possible, and why the משנה needed 'all of it is mine.'

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, indeed (agreeing before adding a point)
Everyday language, how people normally talk

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה needs both 'I found it' and 'all of it is mine.' In everyday speech, 'I found it' can mean just 'I saw it.' The extra words show that seeing alone does not acquire a lost object.

phrases.english: Yes, 'and you found it' of the verse
means that it came into his hand,
but the משנה used everyday language,
and once he sees it, he says: I found it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אֲתַאי לִידֵיהּ
phrases.english: and even though it did not come into his hand,
[I would think] he acquires by mere seeing.
[So] it teaches: 'All of it is mine,'
[to show] that one does not acquire it by mere seeing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 and keeps the answer of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart the Torah's precise language from everyday speech
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק's 'found' means holding, the משנה's 'found' must also mean holding
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks like ordinary people, where 'found' can mean seeing, so 'all of it is mine' is needed to teach that seeing does not acquire

steps.title: Why not just say 'All of it is mine'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'All of it is mine' is the key claim, the משנה could drop 'I found it' completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה only say 'All of it is mine' and leave out 'I found it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the earlier question. Before, it asked why we need 'All of it is mine.' Now it asks why we need 'I found it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the גמרא said that 'All of it is mine' is what teaches that seeing does not acquire. If those are the important words, 'I found it' seems to add nothing. So why not write only 'All of it is mine'?

keyTerms.meaning: So let it teach (a suggestion that the משנה should have been worded differently)

phrases.english: But let it teach 'All of it is mine'
and it would not need 'I found it'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 10 and asks the reverse question about the other half of the claim.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the words 'I found it' within the combined claim, given that 'All of it is mine' carries the lesson (steps 8 and 10)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'All of it is mine' carries the lesson, then 'I found it' is extra and should be left out.

steps.title: Both phrases are needed to teach that seeing does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: Without 'I found it' here, we would think that wherever a משנה says 'found' it means seeing. Writing both phrases shows that seeing alone does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה only said 'All of it is mine,' I would think that in general, whenever a משנה says 'I found it,' a person acquires just by seeing. So the משנה wrote 'I found it' and then added 'All of it is mine.' The extra words teach us that seeing does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'I found it' has to be there. Only when both phrases appear together do the extra words show us that seeing is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary people say 'I found it' as soon as they see something (step 10). If the משנה had left those words out, we could still think that other places that say 'found' mean acquiring by seeing. By writing 'I found it' and then adding 'All of it is mine,' the משנה shows that finding in the sense of seeing does not give ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: And then it taught (it went on to add)
Extra wording in the משנה that is there to teach something

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets down a basic rule of acquiring a lost object: just seeing it does not make it yours.

phrases.english: If it had taught only 'All of it is mine'
I would have said:
in general, where it teaches 'I found it'
phrases.notes: He means other places, outside this משנה, that use the word 'found.'

phrases.english: one acquires through mere seeing.
So it taught 'I found it'
and then taught 'All of it is mine'
because from the extra wording of the משנה it teaches us
that seeing does not acquire.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the wording is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without 'I found it,' we would think 'found' elsewhere means acquiring just by seeing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both phrases are needed. The extra wording teaches that seeing does not acquire.

steps.title: The משנה clearly gives two separate statements
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'this one says' before each phrase, so it is describing two claims and not one combined claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how can you say the משנה teaches only one claim? It says 'this one' and 'this one' again: 'This one says I found it, and that one says I found it; this one says All of it is mine,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the whole 'one claim' reading from step 6. The משנה's own wording seems to show two separate statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each person made a single claim, 'I found it and all of it is mine,' the משנה would introduce it only once. Instead it repeats 'זה אומר' before each phrase. That looks like two different claims, which knocks down the reading used in steps 6 to 12.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This one' and 'this one,' the two people in the dispute
And so on (the rest of the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: This question does not argue that seeing acquires. It only challenges the idea that the משנה describes one claim per person.

phrases.english: But can you really say it teaches one claim?
But it teaches 'this one' and again 'this one':
'This one says: I found it,
and that one says: I found it;
this one says: All of it is mine,' and so on.
phrases.notes: The 'זה אומר' coming back a second time is the whole point. It starts a new statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 6 and challenges its starting point.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that the משנה teaches one combined claim per person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The repeated 'זה אומר' shows two separate statements, so it cannot be one claim.

steps.title: First part is a found object, second part is a purchase
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא (or רב שימי בר אשי, or an unnamed opinion) explains that the two statements describe two different cases: finding and buying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said, and some say רב שימי בר אשי said, and some say it was said without a name: The first part of the משנה is about a found object. The last part is about buying and selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that there are two separate statements and explains that each one is a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I found it' is a case of מציאה, where two people pick up a found object. 'All of it is mine' is a case of מקח וממכר, where each person says he is the one who bought the item. In both cases the item is held by both and they split it.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (another opinion about who said it)
The first part of a משנה
The last part of a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading: 'I found it' = a found object (מציאה). 'All of it is mine' = a purchase (מקח וממכר). These are two cases with the same ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said,
and some say it was Rav Shimi bar Ashi,
and some say it was said without a name:
The first part is about a found object,
and the last part is about buying and selling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ כְּדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by dropping the 'one claim' reading and splitting the משנה into two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the משנה into two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two phrases were one claim about a single found object.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two cases: the רישא is a found object, the סיפא is a purchase.

steps.title: Both cases are necessary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that the משנה needs to teach both the finding case and the buying case.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to explain why we could not learn one case from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה has been split into two cases, someone could ask why it needs both if the ruling is the same. 'וצריכא' says that each case teaches something the other one could not. The explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both cases are needed)
